title: Visiting Zutty Singleton in New York
summary: Lovett saw Zutty Singleton, frail and trembling, on his last New York trip, and recalls him lifted onto the Carnegie Hall stage.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I think he taught us all how to play cymbals.
Yes, Jo, is the cymbal man but he says I have faster hands than him, that's what he says.

Yeah, well Zutty Singleton always said you were very fast. You know, Zutty speaks so highly of your drumming but he speaks very highly of Sidney Catlett but may God rest his soul, Sidney used to say, "The greatest drummer he ever knew was Zutty Singleton". He learned everything from Zutty. Big Sid.
Yeah, Zutty was a wonderful man.
He still is. He's had another stroke, unfortunately.
I went to see him in New York, man.
When did you see him?
Oh, the last time I was in New York.
Well, I told you where he was living. They tore it down so He was living at the Alvin and then he moved toward Woodward.
I went out to his house.
His apartment in the hotel, right on 52nd Street.
No, he was in a home -- had a home
now there.
A nursing home?
No, unless he was just renting there but anyway he and his wife --
Margie.
-- we went out to see he and his wife. This was in a home. Well I'll say dwelling, just like my home.
Well --
I met him there, you know, and he was understand in awful shape, you know what I mean, just trembling like that all the time man.
How long ago was that?
Last time when I was in New York, last year.
Last year.
Yeah, and he came down to Carnegie Hall, man, and they lifted him up on the bandstand so they could introduce him, you know what I mean. Pitiful sight, man.
He's a great one.
Yeah.
